title: Existence of a normalized integral tensor tower comparison
statement: Fix a prime l, a finite extension E of Q_l, and a scheme W, with independent site and coefficient universes. Let R_W be the completed integral coefficient sheaf, S_n its (n+1)st finite quotient, and reduction and total tensor be the recorded constructions of def-pur-integral-derived-operations. There exists a natural isomorphism from the strict global reduction tower of Tot(P tensor_R Q) to the strict tower Res_n Tot(P_n tensor_(S_n) Q_n), natural in unbounded complexes P,Q. On each (p,q) summand over V, its nth component sends s tensor (x tensor y) to (s tensor x) tensor (1 tensor y), for every finite coefficient section s. This asserts existence; uniqueness among normalized ambient-module tower comparisons is established separately.

source.place: Tag 03EL, balanced tensor scalar extension; sites-cohomology.tex Tag 07A4; Bhatt–Scholze Definition 3.4.10, compatible quotient towers.

proof.text: Use the normalized finite total-tensor comparisons of lem-pur-integral-tensor-reduction-tower-comparison. Their maps and inverses commute with differentials and both input chain maps. A pure summand with coefficient one maps to the tensor of the two reduced unit-coefficient summands.

For each consecutive coefficient quotient, lem-pur-integral-tensor-transition-compatibility identifies the two composites. Apply NatTrans.ofOpSequence to the finite comparisons, then componentwise invertibility and naturality assemble a natural isomorphism of the strict unrestricted towers. The nth component is the restriction of the nth finite comparison.

Identify the global slice reduction tower with the unrestricted tower by the recorded scalar-extension object and map equations from def-pur-integral-derived-operations. Its components are identities and preserve all scalar generators. Whisker this comparison by total tensor.

The finite comparison is linear over the finite coefficient sheaf. Write s tensor z as s times (1 tensor z), apply finite linearity, and use bilinearity in the first finite tensor factor. This extends unit-coefficient normalization to arbitrary finite s before restriction of scalars. Substituting the explicit components of the assembled comparison gives the claimed formula.

lean.statement:
theorem normalizedIntegralTensorTower (W : Scheme.{t}) :
    ∃ d : (coefficientTotalTensor.{u, t + 1, t} (ProEt.topology W)
      (completedIntegralCommRingSheafUnrestricted l E W) ⋙
        IntegralOnSlice.tower l E W none) ≅ integralOperationsTensorTowerFunctor l E W,
      ∀ (P Q : CochainComplex (integralTowerModules l E W) ℤ) (n : ℕ) (p q : ℤ)
        (V : W.ProEtᵒᵖ) (s : (integralCoefficientCommRingSheaf l E W n).obj.obj V)
        (x : (P.X p).val.obj V) (y : (Q.X q).val.obj V),
        (((d.hom.app (P, Q)).app (op n)).f (p + q)).val.app V
          (IntegralOnSlice.generator l E W none n _ V s
            (coefficientTensorGenerator.{u, t + 1, t} (Scheme.ProEt.topology W)
              (completedIntegralCommRingSheafUnrestricted l E W) P Q p q (p + q) rfl V x y)) =
          integralOperationsTotalTensorSection l E W n P Q p q V
            (unrestrictedIntegralTensorSection l E W n (P.X p) V s x)
            (unrestrictedIntegralTensorSection l E W n (Q.X q) V 1 y)
